title: Driveclub
subtitle: A road race with a shared result
summary: Driveclub is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 4 racing game, first released in North America on 7 October 2014. Its road events combine a direct driving model with the idea of a club whose members contribute to a common reputation. Races, time trials and drifting challenges take place along routes in several countries. The cars remain the central attraction, but the presentation also pays attention to the landscape, light and weather surrounding them. Driving a clean section can matter alongside the position reached at the finish line.
body: Driveclub is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 4 racing game, first released in North America on 7 October 2014. Its road events combine a direct driving model with the idea of a club whose members contribute to a common reputation. Races, time trials and drifting challenges take place along routes in several countries. The cars remain the central attraction, but the presentation also pays attention to the landscape, light and weather surrounding them. Driving a clean section can matter alongside the position reached at the finish line.

Optional challenges appear within an event, asking the driver to beat a particular section or performance measure while the larger race continues. These smaller comparisons give a corner or stretch of road a purpose beyond merely reaching the next one. Club progression adds those efforts to a shared total, connecting individual driving with the group's standing. Away from online features, the Tour provides a structured sequence of events. The player learns each car through braking, steering and acceleration rather than managing a detailed simulation of its mechanical systems.

Driveclub launched with serious online problems that damaged a game built around connection and shared progress. Later updates expanded it, including dynamic weather that changed both the appearance and conditions of a route. Critics consistently noted the detailed cars, sound and environments, even when judging its early limitations more harshly. Hybrid supplied the score. Sony closed the servers in March 2020 and removed the game from sale. Its offline events remain separate from the club features that originally gave its title and progression their meaning.
